validators.signal: The highest-value validator in the project. Asserts against content that is easy to break silently and covers four public surfaces plus structured data.
validators.risk: Its assertions are content-coupled, so an information-architecture change tempts weakening them. The Phase 2 strategy forbids that explicitly.

validators.signal: Caught real fail-closed and required-field regressions. Validates behavior, not just rendering.
No caught failures on record, but it is cheap and guards the Pages Function contracts.
Required for a static export project. Confirms every route is emitted.
No caught failures on record. Cheap, keep.
Whitespace only. Subsumed by prettier and lint.
validators.recommendation: Drop from the standard gate list.

validators.signal: Under-run. Skipped during generation 6 despite a shared-surface edit. Effectiveness cannot be judged until it runs consistently.
validators.recommendation: Promote into the standard gate list. W3 moves assessment content and makes it load-bearing.

validators.signal: Run once, during the assessment teaser generation. Effectively dormant.
validators.recommendation: Include in the full-suite run after shared-page or config edits.

validators.signal: Required status check. Its value is structural rather than in caught failures.
The only validator that caught the intake subdomain failure. Local and CI checks all passed while the subdomain was dead. This is the strongest argument for the production-verification rule.
Caught the pending subdomain. Then the finding sat open for six weeks, which is a process failure rather than a validator failure.
validators.recommendation: Under the Phase 2 strategy a pending custom domain is a failed deployment check that blocks phase exit, not a warning.

gaps: No validator covers the MCP contract. scripts/validate-mcp-contract.mjs is required before the endpoint ships.
No validator drives a live endpoint with sequential requests, which is the only way to catch a stateless-handshake failure.
No validator confirms actual email delivery. Every delivery check to date has been fail-closed only.
Nothing enforces that the full local suite runs after a shared-surface edit. Both recorded process misses are of this kind.
